newsitem.title: USA: Wis Energy notified of performance decline.
newsitem.headline: Wis Energy notified of performance decline.

text.p: Wisconsin Electric Power Co, a unit of Wisconsin Energy Corp, said Wednesday the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) notified the utility of a declining performance trend at its Point Beach Nuclear plant.
It said the purpose of an NRC "trending letter" is to allow a utility, under the agency's scrutiny, to take early corrective actions.

The letter does not place Point Beach on the NRC's list of problem plants, known as the Watch List. But it emphasizes performance concerns that, if not corrected, could lead to the plant being named to the Watch List. This includes problems at the plant that led to $325,000 in fines levied in December.
"We take NRC's action very seriously," said Wisconsin Electric president Richard Grigg, who took direct charge of nuclear operations in December 1996.
Grigg said Wisconsin Electric has undertaken a comprehensive effort to improve performance at Point Beach.
"Point Beach remains a safe and efficient plant, but in recent months we have recognized that our performance is not up to our own or the NRC's standards," Grigg added in a statement.
